parin: Quick dump of today's exploratory run for speculative decoding on quant-13b (Q4_0). Posting raw so infra/eval folks can pick up.
parin: Setup summary: fast-path=quant-13b-q4_0, candidate_pool=4, dynamic entropy-ramp (start thresh 2.6, increase 0.2 per 20 tokens), rescoring via cheap fp16 pairwise scorer (forward-only), fallback full fp16 when LLR(top vs second) < 0.9 or consensus_score < 0.7. samples=2k english/dev.
bel: What is consensus_score? new metric?
parin: Yeah, quick idea: consensus_score = fraction of tokens where top-2 candidates agree on token identity over the first 40 tokens of completion. Low consensus -> higher diversity -> we prefer rescoring/fallback.
sam: Top-line latency/cost numbers?
parin: Median response latency reduced ~2.7x relative to full fp16 decode. End-to-end including rescoring ~2.2x. Estimated infra token cost ~0.62x baseline (fast-path + rescoring + small fallback fraction).
bel: Quality? any benchmark hits?
parin: Auto: MMLU paired delta -0.65% (2k small sample), Human spot-check (60 pairs) found 5 truncations and 3 rare-code synthesis bugs (incorrect code snippets that looked plausible). The LLR trigger caught 2/3 of those code errors; rescoring corrected the other.
parin: Command used:
```
redwood-evals run --suite spec-explore:v1 \ 
  --model quant-13b-q4_0-fast --fallback-model fp16-13b \ 
  --spec-candidates 4 --entropy-start 2.6 --entropy-ramp 0.2:20 \ 
  --rescoring-model fp16-13b-scorer --llr-thresh 0.9 --consensus-thresh 0.7 \ 
  --samples 2000 --tag spec-llr-consensus-probe
```
ci-bot: Job jd-9123 created, artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/spec/3267890123/ (paired_metrics.json, candidate_traces.tar.gz)
parin: Observed two interesting failure patterns: 1) long-form chain-of-thought truncation when fast-path greedily ends early; 2) code completion errors where templated tokens repeated across candidates -> consensus_score high but wrong (false confidence).
bel: For the code case consensus is misleading when candidates collude on the wrong token. Maybe combine consensus with embedding-divergence on hidden states to detect collusion?
sam: Embedding-divergence cheap? we can use last-layer pooled vector (CLS-like) and cosine between candidate completions. Should be fairly cheap if batched.
parin: I logged last-layer pooled vectors for candidates; cosine divergence flagged the collusion cases where token-level consensus incorrectly looked confident. Will test composite trigger: (LLR<thresh) OR (consensus<thresh AND embedding_divergence>t).
eva: ops: canary ask?
parin: Recommend small canary: 2% traffic on dedicated for 48h, capture token logits for 0.1% of live requests, store candidate pooled vectors for 0.5% requests. Block criteria: MMLU drop >1.0% with paired bootstrap p<0.01 OR code-synthesis incorrect snippet rate increase >0.25% absolute on our code holdout.
eva: noted. ops-bot: Created ticket RED-2603: "spec-llr-consensus canary + pooled-vec capture" https://jira.redwood/browse/RED-2603
sam: For evaluation, do 10k paired multilingual run stratified by task (qa, code, math, longform). Use paired bootstrap CIs and per-task breakdowns. Also compute sign-test for safety checks.
bel: Also ask human raters to label for "coherent reasoning" vs "truncated reasoning" for 1k paired longform prompts. That will help quantify chain-of-thought failures.
parin: Will schedule 10k run and human eval. Quick ablation I ran: enabling embedding-divergence composite reduced false confidence code cases by ~70% in spot-checks while only increasing fallback rate by ~1.8 percentage points.
sam: Nice. Any runtime perf numbers for embedding cosine step?
parin: Microbench on p3-like instance shows pooled-vector extraction + cosine for 4 candidates adds ~0.03x of a full decode (very cheap) if batched. Looks acceptable.
eva: ops: please add metrics to the canary dashboard: fallback_rate, rescoring_rate, avg_pool_size, perc_requests_with_embedding_divergence, per-task MMLU_delta, code_bad_snippet_rate, latency_p50/p95.
parin: Will add. Also planning a small experiment: rescoring-only mode (no full fallback) where we pick rescored top candidate always; measure how much quality we can recover with zero autoreg fallback cost. If that gets within 0.3% MMLU of baseline, we can ship rescoring-only as a cheaper production mode.
bel: Sounds promising. One more thought: add an "early-accept" fast-path rule: if top candidate prob >0.94 and LLR>1.6 and consensus>0.85 then accept immediately (skip rescoring). That saves extra latency for highly confident cases.
parin: Implemented early-accept in the probe; cut rescoring fraction by ~18% with negligible quality change on spot-checks.
parin: Plan checklist: 1) run 10k stratified paired run (scheduled), 2) prepare 1k longform human eval labeling sheet, 3) wire pooled-vector capture in canary, 4) PR with eval config + rollout guardrails, 5) land runtime feature flag for embedding-divergence trigger and early-accept.
ci-bot: Artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/spec/3267890123/ (paired_metrics.json, pooled_vectors.npy, traces/).
eva: I'll reserve dedicated slice and add the dashboard. ops-bot: Created canary slice RED-2603-slice (2% for 48h).
sam: I'll help with paired bootstrap analysis and per-task breakdown. parin: tagging @bel @eva @sam. If anyone wants raw artifacts, they are at the CI link above. :thumbsup:
